decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: The recognizable international stems follow the bounded borrowing policy and occur alongside an attested number headword. OLP-0007 fixes their basic scope. OLP-0043 constructs each rational as an equivalence class of integer pairs with nonzero second coordinate, defines arithmetic and order on representatives, and embeds each integer as the class of its pair with 1. These exact sets and operations come from the source definitions and formulas rather than the canon; no native Javanese foundations attestation is claimed.

decisions.chosen_javanese: enumerasi; bisa didhaptar; enumerabilitas; bisa dietung (countable sense, source-defined)
decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: The canon directly supports general number/count vocabulary and scholarly prose, not countable infinity or enumeration theory. OLP-0027 preserves the elementary list-or-surjection-from-positive-integers approach and the attributed bijection-with-Nat-or-an-initial-segment alternative. OLP-0029 controls the family by an informal list with every member at a finite position, a formal surjection from positive integers for nonempty sets, a separate empty-set case, the equivalent natural-number and finite-initial-segment formulations, and an explicit equation between the tokenized enumerable label and bisa didhaptar. OLP-0031 keeps enumerable unions distinct from finite unions and explicitly states the needed choice assumption for an arbitrary indexed family. OLP-0038 gives the set-theoretic alternative directly: an enumeration is a bijection whose domain is either all natural numbers or a finite initial segment, while the empty set is handled separately; the equivalent natural-number surjection and injection characterizations remain explicit. OLP-0039 proves non-enumerability by showing that every proposed Nat-indexed list omits a constructed element, for both infinite binary sequences and the powerset of Nat. decisions.chosen_javanese: padha cacahe; gedhene himpunan; ora luwih gedhe tinimbang; luwih cilik tinimbang
decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: General cacah and number vocabulary support only ordinary counting language. OLP-0035 defines padha cacahe exactly by a bijection and verifies the equivalence-relation laws. OLP-0036 defines ora luwih gedhe tinimbang by an injection and luwih cilik tinimbang by an injection with no bijection, with the needed Choice qualification on its unrestricted non-enumerability characterization. decisions.english_term_or_issue: numbers or relations are sets, metaphysically speaking; treat them as sets; embed their theories
decisions.chosen_javanese: wilangan utawa relasi iku himpunan saka sisi metafisika; nganggep wilangan utawa relasi minangka himpunan; nyisipake teori-teorine
decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: OLP-0013 distinguishes a metaphysical identity assertion from the weaker mathematical practice of treating certain relations as sets. OLP-0046 makes the parallel distinction for numbers: alternative ordered-pair implementations produce different set objects, natural zero is not literally the constructed integer zero, and the warranted conclusion is only that set theory lets us treat the numbers as sets and embed their theories. OLP-0053 adds that any Dedekind algebra exemplifies the desired natural-number structure and that all such algebras are isomorphic, while expressly withholding an answer about which objects are the natural numbers; the embedding is also conditional on a Dedekind-infinite set. General relasi, wilangan, konteks, and teori have canon support, while no Javanese canon source is claimed to settle the philosophy of mathematics.

decisions.english_term_or_issue: closure; closed under the successor function
decisions.chosen_javanese: tutupan; katutup marang fungsi panerus
decisions.chosen_sense_and_constraints: OLP-0051 defines X as f-closed exactly when every f(x) for x in X remains in X, and defines the closure of o as the intersection of all such sets containing o. The lemma proves containment of o, closure and leastness; JV-D063 makes explicit its self-map scope. OLP-0054 generalizes from one generator to a subset and uses that closure in the Schröder-Bernstein sandwich proof; JV-D064 states the corresponding self-map and carrier-subset scope needed by the generalized definition and lemma. Tutupan and katutup transparently distinguish the generated object from the preservation property; the canon supports general function, member and scholarly-definition language but does not attest this specialist closure terminology.
